newsitem.title: USA: Calif. releases 1997 field crop acreage estimates.
newsitem.headline: Calif. releases 1997 field crop acreage estimates.

text.p: California growers planted more acreage to oats, corn, rice, American Pima cotton, sugar beets and dry edible beans this year than last, the state Department of Food and Agriculture said Tuesday.
Plantings of wheat, upland cotton and barley decreased, it said, releasing crop acreage estimates compiled by the California Agricultural Statistics Service from survey data taken on June 1.

An estimated 230,000 acres were seeded to barley for all purposes in California this year, down 18 percent from 1996, the department said. A total of 180,000 acres is expected to be harvested for grain, down 18 percent from 1996.

Total planted acreage of corn for all purposes was estimated at 580,000 acres, 21 percent above last year. California farmers expect to harvest 260,000 acres of corn for grain in 1997, an 18 percent increase from 1996, it said.

California's cotton growers planted 880,000 acres of upland cotton and 185,000 acres of American Pima cotton in 1997. Upland acreage was down 12 percent, but American Pima was up 12 percent from 1996, it said. Total cotton plantings were down 9 percent from last year, it said.
An estimated 130,000 acres in California were seeded to dry edible beans for the 1997 season, a 2 percent increase from last year's total.

California growers expect to harvest alfalfa from 970,000 acres in 1997, up 3 percent from 1996. The estimate for all other hay to be harvested was 520,000 acres, up 2 percent from last year's total, the department said.
Oats were seeded on 350,000 acres for 1997, up 17 percent from last year's total acreage. Area expected to be harvested for grain totaled 30,000 acres, unchanged from 1996, it said.

California's seeded rice acreage was estimated at 515,000 acres, 3 percent above last year's 502,000, it said. The acreage planted to long grain rice totaled 6,000 acres, up 20 percent; medium grain 491,000, up 1 percent; and short grain, 18,000 acres up 38 percent from 1996.
California has 110,000 acres planted to sugar beets, 31 percent above the total planted in 1996.
California's winter wheat seeded acreage was 510,000 acres, 20 percent below last year's total. The 380,000 acres for grain harvest were 31 percent below last year, the department said.

California's durum wheat planted acreage was estimated at 130,000 acres, down 7 percent from the 140,000 acres seeded last year. The 130,000 acres for grain harvest were down 6 percent from the 138,000 acres harvested last year, the department said.
